newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS - Eurobourses mixed, worried about inflation.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - Eurobourses mixed, worried about inflation.

text.p: European stocks put in a mixed performance on Wednesday with Wall Street's record-breaking pace overnight counter-balanced by the re-emergence of inflation worries.
On currency markets, the dollar was weaker after Bank of Japan Governor Yasuo Matsushita said Japan's economic recovery appeared to be firming and industrial output was on an upward trend.

Frankfurt made the best showing, boosted by New York's 40th record close of the year at 6,397.60 points. German Stocks climbed by 0.5 percent but London and Paris were down with investors jittery over inflationary pressures.

London's FTSE index slipped 0.25 percent as investors were sent scurrying to the sidelines by stronger-than-expected October retail sales and money supply growth, which re-ignited fears of higher interest rates.

The market, already anxious about prospects for the British budget on Tuesday, was alarmed after a 10.3 percent rise in M4 money supply, a big leap in bank and building society lending and the largest rise for two years in three-month figures for retail sales.
"The bank lending figures were far too high. Everyone is worried about sterling's strength, an imminent rate rise and the budget," one dealer said.
Traders said the market was paying little heed to a string of strong performances and favourable earnings, preferring to fret about the larger economic picture.

In Frankfurt, shares climbed because of the Wall Street surge but lost some of the gains after a jump in the October business climate index measured by Germany's Ifo think-tank undermined lingering hopes of an interest rate cut.
The respected economics institute said its October survey showed a higher-than-expected jump in the business climate index last month to 97.4 percent from 95.7.
"The Ifo index was more or less stable but now there is a decent improvement," said one trader, adding that this had eroded hopes of a rate cut.
The figures pushed the computerised IBIS index into the minus column, but floor trading was holding up well by lunch time.
In Paris, French stocks gave up initial gains as bond prices fell on the German Ifo survey, which revived inflation worries.

The dollar was weaker but off its lows against the yen caused by Matsushita's comments after Japan's Finance Minister Hiroshi Mitsuzuka tempered the yen bullishness by saying he believed long-term rates were reflecting economic fundamentals.

Against the mark, the dollar fell half a pfennig after the German business survey. "I am a bit surprised by the strength of this number. Hopes for a further rate cut (right now) will fade away," Guenter Redeker at Chase Manhattan in London said.
An already robust pound strengthened on market speculation of rate rises after the British retail sales and money supply figures.
Sterling was trading at $1.6789 at the European midsession compared to $1.6760 late on Tuesday. The currency earlier hit $1.6820, its best level since October 1992.
Foreign exchange traders were meanwhile switching their attention to U.S. September trade figures due out at 1330 GMT for clues on the health of the American economy.
CURRENCIES AT 1220 GMT
The dollar was quoted at 111.15 yen and 1.4997 marks, compared with 111.55 yen and 1.5036 marks in late European trade on Tuesday.
STOCK MARKETS AT 1220 GMT
LONDON - The Financial Times-Stock Exchange index of 100 leading British shares was down 9.3 points at 3,968.8.
PARIS - The CAC-40 share index was down 7.10 points at 2,232.95.
FRANKFURT - The 30-share DAX index was up 10.64 points at 2,774.73.
PRECIOUS METALS
Gold fixed $378.60 an ounce, compared to Tuesday's close of $378.45. Silver was at $4.90, up one cent.
